rows.text: The two reused modules (response gate and input contract) are byte-identical both to the new PIPELINE_PACKAGE.json pins and to the already-staged prior-round copies, so this round consumed the accepted validator rather than a local substitute.

The dirty-day consistency check compares the full-refresh tip against the validated reply for the same day before assemble_candidate is reachable. A tip that disagrees with the validated reply raises DIRTY_REQUEST_DAY_VALUES_CONFLICT, and the test asserts the downstream merge was not called.

Failure-order controls assert non-invocation directly: a numeric date axis, a missing security and an fq mismatch each stop before assemble_candidate, verified with a patched downstream sentinel rather than by inferring from the exception.
A prior overlap equal to or after the requested day is rejected (OVERLAP_MUST_PRECEDE_REQUEST_DAY); duplicate-day precedence is not guessed anywhere in the chain.
The dirty-history regression control is rejected by the real candidate_merge (DIRTY_HISTORY_KEY_REGRESSION), not by a mock, so the parent-key retention rule is enforced by the module that would run.

The chain returns exactly five stage names ending in PUBLICATION_NOT_AUTHORIZED and carries historical_input_authority_proven=false, expected_market_universe_proven=false, production_integrated=false, publication_authorized=false.

The guide append is documentation of a recovery-workspace diagnostic. The pinned entry blackbox_operate_r10.py, the normative contracts, the root must-read files, the live updater and the historical originals were not touched (entry pin unchanged).

A synthetic in-memory pass is neither a repaired real-data source nor an admitted engine; no malformed RAW file was supplied, no request binding was manufactured for one, no date was derived from a filename and no factor was filled.
